And on a side note, walking besides a long straight road a dragonfly crashed its face into a vehicle... Wounded somehow and perhaps even blinded, the beast in flight kept buzzing endlessly, but facing the ground, rubbing it in, with no way out... I was just listening to music (Spor - Aztec) and with my hands and legs shimmering along these fast lanes I started shuffling and stomping, until out of a sudden I have made a hole in the ground.

There's only that many moves a walking person can do with their feet; one that wants to deliver himself to another place at a fast pace.

Going to mountains is joyful and inspiring. It used to be mystical -- the view is magical, when the mist blurs out the endless horizon.

These days storytelling became more demanding on spacewalkers; it's not just enough to take a picture of a hiking attire that the most creative sky-gliding adventurer would conceive in a fantasy realm. Outfit is now interlaced with technology, if embraced within the fabric or not -- and miracles won't just start up by jumping off a cliff. 

So save it; going for it starts while waking up, first off.

A summary of happenings during my (@BlaÅ¾ Beuermann writing) brief visit to Creative Climate Leadership in Ankaran...
I had been offline for most of the summer, just briefly checking Facebook and Gmail. I had not been forwarded the invitation to the conference week, though I did know one of the organizers, @Ema Weixler and a participant, @Gaja MeÅ¾nariÄ Osole who was my last girlfriend. Recently we had been seeing each other again and she has invited me to her grandmother's 88th birthday near Pula, Crotia. I took with me a bicycle, planning to travel back to Ljubljana, during the weekend asking Gaja if I could join the first evening, but she refused saying that she wants independence and the week for herself. Instead, she gave me a third option, a way out for her, to stay with her father and grandmother until tuesday.
This was after we had some chats with her father @Max Osole, on many topics (from pig organ stem cells being grown in chicken that he said a muslim imam has approved, to a fun project that he invited me to on topic of confusing digital algorithms with fake data, to our common acquaintance, Gaja). With her grandmother we also had some funky moments, she said one thing I wouldn't state here, but after the clash with Gaja we also spoke about me and her - how she needed security and solid ground and that's when her father joined in. I couldn't help but notice how she has been rejecting most of my initiatives to engage with her work-wise (and her father has also experienced this) - if I was a bit pushy I do appologize - but as I have said, I have been giving her best of my mental strength to support her while she navigated through struggles, but yet I am left here with nothing to show from our time together, while she has made great advances in her career. She wouldn't even support me by reading my Facebook wall and giving a like or comment once in a while. It is as if I was an object she put up with, because I had become known for my social media outbreak and Good will gesture project I carried with me, a potential suspect for her invasive plant metaphor. And as her grandmother (and admittedly, my own mother, too) would put it, one needs to take care of self, first.
I decided to call up my mother's partner Raul who lives on the seaside in Slovenia and sleep over before cycling back to Ljubljana, leaving the party and going solo, just as it has happened to me. Gaja left in a rush and as I had been mounting wheels to my mother's bicycle while cooking a vegan pasta to energize myself for the road, I was being persuaded by grandmother and father to stay, and soon enough Gaja came back. So we ate our lunch, me having just the salad, swimming in the pool she reversed her statement saying "I want you to come" and soon we drove off in silence.
Having arrived to Ankaran my phone's battery was almost done and I decided to leave the place as my trousers had oil stains. Finding my way to city of Koper, I turned on my phone in front of a McDonalds in a shopping district there, but it wouldn't stay up long enough for me to call Raul. I had to bike back to her hotel and got lucky enough to get to call Raul from the reception. What a surprise, he had taken off with his car to intercept me on my way, so I didn't struggle in the dark.
Gaja had passed by while I was waiting, walking from a small room in the lobby in company of other participants, not seeing me. When Raul came I called her from his phone and we met for a small beer. We shared some stories and as we were departing, Gaja offered me to sleep there, but Raul insisted that I went with him - so I did.
I woke up the next day, thinking about the situation. I decided to give myself a tour of the city, exploring it like a foreigner would. I sat in a cafe with wifi internet near the train station almost ready to depart, drinking espresso and natural juice, when my mother had sent me an email - Raul had his birthday that day. So should I stay a day more? I picked up information on departures from the train station and moved back to his apartment and soon enough he came back, as he had plans for his birthday.
I went around some more, bicycling to find lunch, but the place that Raul recommended was being renovated, due to open the next day. And my left leg hurt me, so I thought maybe I could leave the bike with Gaja, maybe it would've come useful to her. Sun was slowly fading as I came to the reception to leave her a key, tools, a light and a note. But then I thought, is she's the only one to have the bicycle there and is there a way for other participants to rent bikes, too? I asked at the reception, but they said it's not possible at this time of the year. I asked some locals and they said that bike service there as well as Koper were both closed.
And then I left, curiously exploring partizan monuments, and the salt bay nearby, picking up two plants and four shelves. I was walking back over a bridge as the sun was fading, a lovely view. I stopped over to get a small snack (generous fries in McDonalds) and three beers at a gas station, just in case we gathered on that night with Raul and maybe Gaja. I had a snack and a drink on the beach as locals were jogging and passing by in chatter. Soon after I had returned Raul also came back, we were watching television while he had been speaking for a long time on phone and then later we had a chat about renting bicycles from those who are selling them online - he thought this wasn't easily possible. I also spoke with Gaja then and she explained to me her experience and what they were doing. And I told her about what was on the television and later messaged her with my idea to find the bicycles. And the next day I thought I would surely go back, early in the morning, at 5.25.
Raul woke me up, but I decided to wait a little more, at least until the next train. Then I went for a coffee and a natural juice again to a different place, where I saw Sixt handball player team and I borrowed a lighter for my cigarette while reading a newspaper I had recently scanned and summarizing it for Gaja - maybe she could use some insight into local happenings. Then, just as my laptop battery was almost drained, I got in touch with a bike rental vendor nearby, it suddenly became possible to find bikes for them to rent. I had left some of my belongings at Raul's place and went to pick them up as now I thought I was surely going to catch the train.
But having left my bicycle with Gaja, I was a bit too slow by foot, so instead I would clean Raul's apartment as a favor to him. Just as I was almost finished he came back and soon after he had to leave. I went to the cafe from my second day, next to the train station, thinking, should I catch a bus to Ankaran or go straight home? Meanwhile, Gaja responded, she said that the bike tour didn't fit the event's stuffed programme and I saw that I had maybe just enough time to pick up the bicycle with a bus, drive back and catch the train. As I had internet I sent the details on whereabouts of bike rentals and their capacities to Julie's bicycle, one of the organizers of the course. I also sent SMS to Gaja and Raul and headed off, again offline. I came there and I saw Gaja couldn't make it on time so I knew I wouldn't make the train that day.
And a bit later she came back and we had a beer or two. She told me about her daily activities - though she had missed some sessions (morning or noon, I can't remember for sure) due to picking up her friend from London college in Koper, having been "pounded by a mosquito until 4 am" and then having lunch in Koper with him (order of speach). She had a nice experience on that day - connection and purpose, touching with fingers with eyes closed, each humbling their unique sound, recognizing each other in the room. At the time she had just come from a meeting with a core team, she said. Some of her colleagues came by, inviting her to Trieste, but she said she was too tired. She asked me "Would you drive? I'm too tired", I said sure, lets go. But then she decided not to go, anyway. "But you can go". I went to her room to pick up the bike gear and we gave each other kisses on cheeks as I left.
I had seen a car departing and I swiftly ran to it just as it had almost left. One of the organizers from Slovenia was driving there and he asked if I could take my own car and maybe one of the ladies, but I said "no, no", so he moved a child chair to the trunk. It was pretty exciting to meet with course participants, one coming from Australia, others from Europe, some of them speaking awfuly many languages, and boy was that a fast car. We walked through Trieste, stopping for historical insights at glorious monuments by the sea (our slovene guide's family was living in Trieste). So we stopped for a beer in city centre, near a street which was a few years ago occupied at night by homeless people, many of them drug addicts. There's only layers of wood over windows and doors on some buildings now, reminding of that time. Well, (un)fortunate for me, I only had enough money for that train ticket in the morning - but they had granted me a small beer. Our chat, full of gesturing, had went astray when I had told them some stories about me and my quirky shopping behaviors - apparently I should see a therapist, said the slovene as we were already leaving.
Afterwards they moved into their own circles, as they were during the course, walking back to the car. We made a small detour to a castle hill to find a leapfrog there, that small guy was already used to human presence, when the lady from Australia touched it, it would barely move. And so we went back, saying "see you tomorrow" and I said "see you today". I went along with the ladies to picked up my stuff from a hidden spot under Gaja's staircase and we were commenting on all the empty room in the campus, how easy it would be for some migrants and alike to hop in when in need, and then we split.
I waited in the restaurant, thinking it might be easier to just stay up for this short time I had before my train came. I wrote a few thoughts and sent SMS to Gaja about my whereabouts, but she was probably already asleep, and then I notified Raul if he can leave keys somewhere outside and email me somehow in case I came back. It was almost 1 am when he came over to pick me up, but I said I would just wait there.
So there I was and at about 2 am I decided to knock on Gaja's door. It was late and I was worried about it, but I thought it would be nice to share a good mood with her and just sleep a bit - maybe even stay for the day, if I felt they wanted me there. After 5 knocks she opened the door, but her face was cold. I came in and thought I will just leave her to get rest, but she kept sighing in annoyance, even though I was being completely silent. I asked, "do you want me to leave, I don't want to disturb you with my presence", but she wouldn't make this decision for me. What could I do? I was leaving, hearing her say "you victim, victim, victim" as I was closing the door.
I sat again at the reception, later headed to check Facebook. She was yelling at me through chat at 4 am. On her wall she has uploaded a few videos, on topic of (not actually) loving what we eat, a female activist group in Africa, an old lady telling her love story (and how she let go of her man) and a seashell plastic catastrophe video. I waited until my train and left.
Next day I missed most of my day, feeling crushed. In the evening I responded to her mentor/therapist, wanting to cancel any further meetings and she responded to me privately that she would cancel any of our further meetings. So there we are. She said I could let her know where I was, ask her if I could come to her place, instead of knocking... I didn't agree with her statements on Facebook and I don't agree with them now, and her gestures to help me by sending me links after so many opportunities have been taken by her, excluding possibility to join in, I think I will pass this kind of charity to cover up her manipulations.
I have deactivated my Facebook, because as the feedback there shows, my effort serves noone. And also, Julie's bicycle didn't write back, but well their slovene partners would probably be able to find a place to rent bikes themselves, too. I think they probably knew me through Ema, hence the unprovoked psychiatrist statement.

New year ...

I'm grateful for spending it in the mountains with Gaia and a few other people, where we shared many moments. From dinners that we shared, some eating veggies and others meat, too, to conversations and nights that we shared. Our host, Mr. K., he lives in a remote place, where you can see Italian see and Slovenian hills on a crisp day, where wind brings in fresh air, sunsets come saturated and stars shine bring in the night.

On new year's eve when we wandered around the hills to visit the highest peak and a few people, he was so happy about sharing this experience with us that he knealed and kissed the earth saying Allah.

There is only a few residents on the hills, scattered yet connected, with word of mouth, a strong mobile network and also by sharing their produce, gathering and socializing. With our host we would smoke everything inside, while this is not the habit everywhere. Some people are really relaxed there, losing some of reservations, sometimes scratching themselves as we city people only do alone.

We had a homemade tea and schnaps with a joyful older man who had a funny accent. Later we went on to meet L., a programmer who connects to an optic cable up in the hills, and as he mentioned without earlier reference, maybe even to a telepathic network, but not to Facebook. We eventually ended up spending our new year's eve together at K.'s place. Me and Gaia fell asleep even before midnight, but we were both awake to hear the sad news about the jihadist Santa Claus bomber in Turkey around 4 am on the radio, which was otherwise casually discussing last year's outs and abouts.

Next day we gathered for a dinner at a healer's home, who offers his hands and energy to people in need of a rest and sometimes also one of his guestrooms to friends passing by. He had been reading up on Transsurfing, a way to experience realities of our own desire without any guilt from side effects of as karma. This took us into a philosophical discussion of many sudden insights, some incomprehensions, bananas, and a question - where does an insight come from? 

On our last evening I had finally learned to make apple pie, I was kneading dough in a company of K. and his friend L. and it took many shapes in the process, from a long roll to a shape of fertile thighs. It was made with olive oil! Soon enough we could taste it together.

During the night as I was sleeping alone by the fireplace on the lowest floor, while the fire was slowly burning out the wind blowing was coming in strong, in shocks, pushes. It was as if the top floor was in quake and people up there were awake. Moaning as if they were enjoying something new, I almost wanted to go up there and check, but had swiftly changed my mind.

In the morning the conversation was casual. From the conversation about the heard voices of the night we moved on to discuss the floor, which was carefully and well made, some of it of stone and the rest of wood which loudly spoke it's wisdom, gathered through the years.

In case we stayed for a day more, Gaia said jokingly that it's now my (our) turn to switch beds with K.. But it was already time to go back to the city and start the new year.
